user_query: Applicant has just been picked up on the hotline and has described a matter. How do I triage?
variations: New applicant, what do I do?
Applicant is asking for legal help, where do I start?
How do I figure out which scheme applies?
First call of the day — walk me through the initial questions.
part_a_general_info: This is the master triage entry. Every new applicant who presents a legal matter begins here. Your job is to assess, in sequence: (1) whether the applicant is already legally represented; (2) whether the applicant is the affected party or a third party; (3) whether the matter is a business/commercial dispute; (4) whether the applicant has already received legal advice on the same matter; and (5) what type of matter it is (criminal, family/matrimonial, civil). Each branch leads to a Route defined in Part C. Pro Bono SG provides legal help to individuals who are not able to afford legal services, through legal guidance (free) and legal representation (free to low-cost), on their personal legal issues. Key scheme taxonomy you must know: Pro Bono SG Schemes • Legal Clinics (guidance): Free 20-minute legal consultations. For low to median-income individuals (regardless of nationality). • Community Law Centre (guidance): Free 30-minute legal consultations for vulnerable individuals (violence victims, persons with disabilities, elderly, language barrier, etc.). For low to median-income individuals (regardless of nationality). • Urgent Legal Consultation (guidance): Free same-day legal consultations for urgent matters (e.g. court date within 14 days, appeals, imminent deportation, imminent loss of shelter). For low to median-income individuals (regardless of nationality). • CLAS (representation): Criminal Legal Aid Scheme — Free to low-cost representation for low-income foreigners facing non-capital criminal charges. • FJSS (Pro Bono) (representation): Free to low-cost representation for low-income foreigners with Singaporean children facing matrimonial proceedings (incl. Syariah). • FJSS (Modest Means): Low-cost representation for individuals facing matrimonial proceedings, who marginally failed the Legal Aid Bureau's or FJSS (Pro Bono)'s means test. Non-Pro Bono SG Schemes • Legal Aid Bureau (representation) – Free to low-cost representation for low-income SGC/PR facing civil and family matters. • Public Defender’s Office (representation) – Free to low-cost representation for low-income SGC/PR facing non-capital criminal charges. • Legal Assistance Scheme for Capital Offences (representation) – Free representation for individuals charged with capital offences. Always listen for urgency cues and vulnerability cues while running these questions. If either surface, cross-reference GEN3-T06 (Urgent Matter) and GEN3-T13 (Vulnerable Applicant) concurrently — do not wait to finish the triage.
triage_questions: Q1: Is the applicant currently represented by a lawyer on this same matter?
Q2: Is the applicant the person who needs legal help, or are they calling on behalf of someone else?
Q3: Is this a business/commercial matter (company dispute, B2B contract, commercial debt, shareholder dispute)?
Q3A (if Q3 = Yes): Is the matter for a non-profit / charity / social enterprise (or someone seeking to incorporate one), or for a for-profit business?
Q4: Has the applicant already received legal advice from a lawyer on this same matter?
Q5: What type of matter is the applicant facing?
branching_logic: Q1: Is the applicant currently represented by a lawyer on this same matter?
If Q1 = Yes → Route A (Already Represented)
If Q1 = No → Proceed to Q2
If Q1 = Not Sure → Clarify: "Are you currently paying a lawyer or has a lawyer filed any documents for you on this matter?" — if still unclear, Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).
Q2: Is the applicant the person who needs legal help, or are they calling on behalf of someone else?
If Q2 = Calling on behalf and person who needs help able to self-help → Route B (Refer Person to Contact PBSG Directly)
If Q2 = Self or calling on behalf and person who needs help unable to self-help → Proceed to Q3
If Q2 = Not Sure → Clarify: "Will you be the named party in any legal proceedings?"; if still unclear, Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).
Q3: Is this a business/commercial matter (company dispute, B2B contract, commercial debt, shareholder dispute)?
If Q3 = Yes → Ask Q3A before routing.
Q3A (if Q3 = Yes): Is the matter for a non-profit / charity / social enterprise (or someone seeking to incorporate one), or for a for-profit business?
If Q3A = Non-profit / charity / social enterprise (or seeking to incorporate one) → Route C (Non-Profit Legal Services)
If Q3A = For-profit business → Route D (Reject — Business/Commercial Matter)
If Q3A = Not Sure → Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).
If Q3 = No → Proceed to Q4

If Q3 = Not Sure → Clarify whether the matter arises in the applicant's personal capacity (e.g. sole proprietor, personal guarantor for company loan or individual facing criminal charge for business-related issue) or as a business, proceed to “Q3 = Yes” or “Q3 = No” options depending on answer. If still unsure, Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).
Q4: Has the applicant already received legal advice from a lawyer on this same matter?
If Q4 = Yes → Ask Q4A: Is the applicant seeking legal guidance (clinic consultation) or legal representation (a lawyer to act on their behalf)?
If Q4A = Guidance → Route E (Reject for Guidance — Prior Advice Received)
If Q4A = Representation → Proceed to Q5 (applicant may still be eligible for representation schemes)
If Q4A = Not Sure / Both / All / "Whatever help I can get" → Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff)
If Q4 = No → Proceed to Q5
If Q4 = Not Sure → Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff).
Q5: What type of matter is the applicant facing?
If Q5 = Criminal (charged with an offence, police investigation, court mention) → Route G (Criminal Stream)
If Q5 = Matrimonial (divorce, custody, maintenance, variation of court orders, including Syariah divorce) → Route H (Matrimonial Stream)
If Q5 = Civil/Others (contract disputes, property, employment, estate/probate, personal injury, neighbour disputes, etc.) → Route I (Civil Stream)
If Q5 = Not Sure → Route F (Escalate to PBSG Staff)

NOTE: If at any point during Q1–Q5 the applicant reveals urgency factors (court date within 14 days, violence, self-harm risk, immigration pass expiring, etc.) → cross-reference GEN3-T06 (Urgent Matter) concurrently.
routing: Route B (Refer Person to Contact PBSG Directly):
Route E (Reject for Guidance — Prior Advice Received):
Route G (Criminal Stream) → Proceed to GEN3-T02 (Criminal Stream Triage).
Route H (Matrimonial Stream) → Proceed to GEN3-T-FAM (Matrimonial Stream Triage).
Route I (Civil Stream) → Proceed to GEN3-T-CIV (Civil Stream Triage).
guardrail: • Under s 33 of the Legal Profession Act 1966, only qualified, practising lawyers may give legal advice. You must NEVER: (a) interpret a legal document for the applicant; (b) apply the law to the applicant's facts; (c) predict the outcome of a case; and (d) tell the applicant what they should do legally. • You MAY: (a) confirm scheme eligibility against objective criteria; (b) read out scheme descriptions verbatim; (c) explain PBSG hotline operations; (d) take down particulars and escalate to PBSG Staff. • If the applicant insists on legal advice, respond: "I'm an intern/volunteer and I'm not able to give legal advice. What I can do is help you find the right legal help avenue or direct you to a qualified lawyer." • If in doubt at any point — escalate to PBSG Staff. • Protect applicant confidentiality. Do not discuss the applicant outside the hotline context. Do not retain personal data on personal devices and/or beyond the PBSG volunteering period.
